payload.friendly_name: Service release line and native packaging
payload.purpose_context: Issues #241 and #71. Operator rulings 2026-10-31 (spec-kitty#6117): a service-v* tag line separate from contract-charter-v*; native per OS for linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos-arm64 and windows-x64 with the jar as fallback at 4.0.0 GA; core pins the service and fetches it on first use. This mission records the ADR, adds the GraalVM native build and smoke test in CI and a service-release workflow; it pushes no tag.
payload.purpose_tldr: The charter service releases on its own service-v* tag line with native binaries for four OS targets plus the jar, checksummed and attested, named as core's pin model expects.

payload.question: D1: service tag form and version scheme?

payload.final_answer: Operator 2026-10-31: service-vX.Y.Z[-pre], pre suffix [0-9A-Za-z.] only; tag equals gradle.properties version (no -SNAPSHOT); service SemVer of its own (major: launcher/operator-visible break; minor: new contract minor or feature; patch: fixes); 0.x until contract 1.0.0; one bundled contract version per release; a pre-release may bundle a -SNAPSHOT contract, a final release requires contract-charter-v<info.version> merged into HEAD.

payload.question: D2: release asset names agreed with core?

payload.final_answer: Operator 2026-10-31: prefix spec-kitty-charter-service kept; raw executables <prefix>-<ver>-{linux-x64,linux-arm64,macos-arm64}, <prefix>-<ver>-windows-x64.exe, <prefix>-<ver>.jar; one .sha256 per asset; SHA256SUMS sorted, bare names; build-provenance attestation; no contract tarballs; --latest=false; -pre makes a pre-release.

Operator 2026-10-31: no blocking change; draft filed as spec-kitty/spec-kitty#6909 (provisional comment, per-service default repository, help texts, attestation verification, and #71's checksum-install criterion).

payload.question: D4a: how is the container profile handled in a native binary?

payload.final_answer: Operator 2026-10-31: option (a), evaluate the container profile at run time in an always-present bean.
Operator 2026-10-31: register it and smoke-test on all four targets; escalate only if the guard smoke is red.
Operator 2026-10-31: two stacked PRs, ADR and docs first.

payload.question: D6: when does the native matrix run?

payload.final_answer: Operator 2026-10-31: reusable service-native.yml on release, push to main and path-filtered PRs; the jar smoke on every PR.

payload.question: D7: which issues does the PR close?

payload.final_answer: Operator 2026-10-31: closes #241, references #71; #71's launcher criterion moves to #70 and its core-verify criterion to spec-kitty#6909.

reason: APPROVE (reviewer-renata) fab81302. Behaviour under the container profile is unchanged: ContainerStartupCheck runs every rule after a matchesProfiles(container) guard (same semantics as @Profile, incl. default profiles); ContainerWiring binds charter.container with Binder.get(env).bindOrCreate + IgnoreTopLevelConverterNotFoundBindHandler + ValidationBindHandler(SpringValidatorAdapter), the same handler chain Boot's ConfigurationPropertiesBinder uses for a @Validated value-object record with its own JSR-303 validator, so the @NotEmpty/@NotBlank property-naming messages and BindValidationException/failure analyzer are unchanged; no secret is a component; both beans have LazyInitializationExcludeFilter (strengthened: the record bean was lazy-skippable before; new lazy test). Without the profile neither binds nor checks (tests assert start passes and properties() empty). Closing the ValidatorFactory after a completed bind is safe (immutable record). Deviation from plan D-2 (ContainerWiring kept instead of deleted, own ValidatorFactory not the context validator) is acceptable: ruling D4a's substance (always-present beans, run-time profile) holds and Boot itself validates @ConfigurationProperties with its own validator, not the context's. NoBuildTimeProfilesTest would fail on the old code (both ArchUnit rules hit the two classes; bean-set test lacks containerWiring/containerStartupCheck without the profile). Checklist: 1 Dead code PASS (ContainerWiring is Spring-registered; properties() is a test-observation seam replacing the former ContainerProperties bean, which also had no production consumer); 2 Synthetic fixture PASS (context-runner and shipped-service starts); 3 Silent empty return PASS (early returns are the documented no-profile path; Optional.empty documented); 4 FR-008 coverage PASS (missing allowed-hosts fails under profile, incl. shipped service; no-profile start passes; bean set identical); 5 Frozen surface N/A; 6 Locked decision PASS; 7 Shared-file ownership PASS with note: ContainerSecretsTest.java is outside WP02's owned_files, a 3-line assertion adaptation forced by removing the ContainerProperties bean, owned by no other WP; WP03 must register BindableRuntimeHintsRegistrar.forTypes(ContainerProperties.class) (ContainerWiring Javadoc relies on it) and its native smoke under the container profile (ADR-0046 d5) must exercise the Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory path; 8 Production fragility PASS (BindException is the documented fail-loud start refusal). Nits, non-blocking: ContainerProperties.java:11 Javadoc line is 153 chars (not reflowed). verifyAll green per /tmp/sk/verify-wp02.log.
